comment: Real engine output of the cards below and the row keys the server numbers, with the LaTeX of each numbered row. The Python tests (test_equation_rows_contract.py, test_equation_rows_variation_stats_expansion.py) check the keys and the rows against the readers; the vitest test checks that the panels put each number on exactly that formula. The handbook `methods` of a card are left out. Regenerate with the helper in the second test file (MINERVA_REGEN_ROW_FIXTURE=1), which adds missing entries and never rewrites one.

methods.title: Numerical integration (initial-value problem)
methods.reason: the highest derivatives can be solved for, so it becomes a first-order system
requires: initial values for every unknown and derivative below its order
the interval of the independent variable
limitations: an approximation on the interval you choose; not exact and not valid beyond it
stiffness cannot be judged in advance: the integrator is chosen from measured behaviour
checked against an independent integrator, tolerance refinement and the equation's defect

methods.title: Local power series about a regular point
methods.reason: the highest derivatives can be solved for, so a Taylor series can be built from the initial values
requires: initial values for every unknown and derivative below its order
limitations: local: valid near the expansion point only, and a singular point is unsupported
the residual is checked through the claimed order

methods.title: Equilibria and local linear stability
methods.reason: autonomous with few states: equilibria, the Jacobian and its eigenvalues
limitations: local and from the linearisation only; it says nothing about global stability
where the linearisation has eigenvalues on the imaginary axis it does not decide

methods.title: Phase plane (direction field and trajectories)
limitations: trajectories are numerical approximations, each checked as in the IVP method

methods.title: Closed-form solution (SymPy), verified by substitution
methods.reason: no solvable class was recognised, so Minerva does not attempt a closed form
limitations: SymPy may fail, or give an implicit or unevaluated form
shown only after substituting back into your equation and checking numerically
the solution may omit singular solutions and is valid only where its restrictions hold

methods.title: Poincaré-Lindstedt (periodic motion, one degree of freedom)
methods.reason: the acceleration depends on the velocity (damping or a gyroscopic term)
requires: a small parameter named by you
limitations: periodic solutions near a stable equilibrium only

methods.title: Regular perturbation expansion
methods.reason: no symbolic parameter to expand in
requires: a small parameter named by you
limitations: valid for small values of that parameter and bounded intervals
secular terms grow with time and can invalidate the expansion for long times

methods.title: Numerical boundary-value solution
methods.reason: needs conditions at two distinct points
requires: a starting guess is chosen by Minerva
limitations: a solution may not exist, may not be unique, and the solver may converge to another one
shown only after the boundary conditions, the residual and a refined mesh agree
